bilingual.notes: Bilingual/Bicultural Education endorsement (code 1480) under N.J.A.C. 6A:9B-11.5. Add-on to a CE, CEAS, or standard NJ instructional certificate. CEAS path: complete a Department-approved bilingual/bicultural preparation program. CE path: 12 credit hours of formal instruction. Target-language proficiency required via a Department-approved nationally recognized oral/written test (or equivalent undergrad/graduate education in the target language).

eld.notes: English as a Second Language endorsement (code 1475) under N.J.A.C. 6A:9B-11.6. Add-on to an underlying NJ instructional certificate. Path A: Department-approved NJ college/university preparation program. Path B: 15 credit hours of formal instruction across seven topic areas. Department-approved nationally recognized test of oral and written English proficiency required. languageProficiency=false because the ESL endorsement is not premised on a non-English target language; the proficiency requirement is English.

sei.notes: No statewide SEI mandate for general classroom teachers. NJ requires ESL teachers to hold an ESL endorsement; LEAs serving 10+ multilingual learners must offer one period daily of ESL by a certified teacher (N.J.S.A. 18A:6-38; N.J.A.C. 6A:9B-11.6).

history.title: New Jersey Bilingual Education Act enacted (P.L. 1974, c. 197)
history.description: P.L. 1974, c. 197, codified at N.J.S.A. 18A:35-15 to -26, required any school district enrolling 20 or more EL students of the same native language to operate a full bilingual education program in that language and English, plus an ESL component for any EL student regardless of language threshold. New Jersey was among the earliest states to mandate bilingual instruction by statute (after Massachusetts 1971, New Mexico 1973, Texas 1973, Illinois 1973). The 1975 statute remains the legal backbone of NJ's bilingual/bicultural and ESL endorsements (N.J.A.C. 6A:9B-11.5 and -11.6) and of the 20-student program-trigger threshold the State still enforces.

history.title: New Jersey State Seal of Biliteracy enacted (P.L. 2015, c. 303)
history.description: Governor signed P.L. 2015, c. 303 on January 19, 2016, creating the New Jersey State Seal of Biliteracy administered by NJDOE. First seals awarded in the 2016-17 school year.

history.title: EPAA 29(100) document analysis (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021)
history.description: Leider, Colombo & Nerlino published in Education Policy Analysis Archives 29(100) a comprehensive document analysis of every state and DC's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI teacher-credentialing requirements, professional teaching standards mentions, and EL-percentage figures, based on primary SEA sources collected October–December 2019. The 2019 coding of New Jersey's EL-credentialing landscape is preserved as a temporally-anchored research baseline against which the catalog's later verifications are framed.

elPercentHistory.note: New Jersey Department of Education, mid-October fall snapshot (151,245 Multilingual Learners of 1,426,840 enrolled). Identification under N.J.A.C. 6A:15: home language survey, records review, and English-language proficiency assessment. The 2023 amendments to N.J.A.C. 6A:15 expanded identification criteria, contributing alongside documented enrollment growth (~94,000 in 2019-20 to over 130,000 in 2023-24) to the 2.4 percentage-point gap from NCES's fall 2021 value (8.2%). New Jersey does not publish a multi-year EL series for fall 2018-2021 in directly accessible form, so methodological continuity with the prior NCES series cannot be confirmed from overlapping observations.
